question: The FEC row stores the primary measurement 78.4 at 296.15 K (Kobayashi 2003) and keeps model_ready=false because the competing 107 leg could not be read. Ue et al. 2014, Chapter 2 of "Electrolytes for Lithium and Lithium-Ion Batteries", was recorded in the manual as blocked behind Springer identity authentication. Is it readable now, and does it state the relative permittivity of FEC?
answer: Yes on both counts. The chapter PDF was retrieved over direct HTTP with status 200 (application/pdf, 73 pages) on 2026-09-25. Table 2.3 "Physical properties of fluorinated solvents" (printed page 101) lists 4-Fluoro-1,3-dioxolan-2-one (FEC), FW 106, d 1.50 g cm-3, eps_r 107, eta 4.1 mPa s, E_HOMO -13.30 eV, E_LUMO 1.45 eV. The chapter states that the physical properties of typical fluorinated compounds were summarised in Table 2.3 from references [4] and [5] (printed page 100), and separately states that the relative permittivity and viscosity of FEC were higher than those of EC (Fig. 2.4a, b) [25] (printed page 105); reference [25] is Hagiyama et al. 2008, Chem. Lett. 37, 210-211 - the paper the dataset already names as the unread primary candidate for the 107 leg. The 107 value is therefore now read, but only at compilation level: Table 2.3 carries no per-row source footnote for FEC, so this chapter is a compilation relaying the Hagiyama line rather than an independent primary measurement. The stored dielectric 78.4, T_K 296.15 and model_ready=false are unchanged.

source.chapter_title: Nonaqueous Electrolytes with Advances in Solvents
source.book_title: Electrolytes for Lithium and Lithium-Ion Batteries
source.access: retrieved over direct HTTP from this network; no login prompt and no paywall interstitial were served
source.extracted_text_sha256_convention: Content hash of the extracted text after normalising CRLF line endings to LF (UTF-8).

evidence.units_and_meaning: eps_r is the relative permittivity (dimensionless); the chapter defines eps_r as relative permittivity on printed page 100.
evidence.temperature_stated_in_source: not stated for the FEC row of Table 2.3
evidence.per_row_footnote: none for the FEC row; footnotes a and b in this table attach to cis-DFEC and to the two perfluoroether rows only
evidence.table_source_attribution: Printed page 100: "The physical properties of typical fluorinated compounds and non-fluorinated counterparts were summarized in Tables 2.3 and 2.4, respectively [4, 5]" - i.e. the table as a whole is attributed to two Sasaki review items, not to a per-molecule primary measurement.
evidence.body_text_attribution: Printed page 105: "The relative permittivity and viscosity of FEC were higher than those of EC (Fig. 2.4a, b) [25]."
evidence.reference_25: Hagiyama, K.; Suzuki, K.; Ohtake, M.; Shimada, M.; Nanbu, N.; Takehara, M.; Ue, M.; Sasaki, Y., Physical properties of substituted 1,3-dioxolan-2-ones, Chem. Lett. 2008, 37, 210-211.
evidence.reference_4: Sasaki, Y., The status and view for fluorine-containing organic solvents, In Advanced battery technologies-2011; The Electrochemical Society of Japan: Tokyo, Japan, 2011; 17-30.
evidence.reference_5: Sasaki, Y., Organic electrolytes of secondary lithium batteries, Electrochemistry 2008, 76, 2-15.
evidence.unrelated_lead_rejected: Reference [57] of the same chapter is Suzuki et al., Physical and electrochemical properties of fluoroacetonitrile, Electrochemistry 2007, 75, 611-614 - fluoroacetonitrile, not 3-methoxypropionitrile. It was checked and rejected as a MOPN lead.

attribution_chain.value_107_seen_in: Ue et al. 2014 Table 2.3 (compilation table), printed page 101
attribution_chain.independent_of_hagiyama_2008: no - the chapter relays the Hagiyama research line; it is not an independent measurement
attribution_chain.primary_measurement_located: no - Hagiyama 2008 itself remains unread (academic.oup.com served HTTP 403; the J-STAGE path served HTTP 404 on this pass)

decision.stored_value_unchanged: dielectric stays 78.4, T_K stays 296.15, model_ready stays false
decision.reason_model_ready_unchanged: The row has one confirmed primary measurement (78.4) and one compilation-level competing value (107) whose named primary candidate is still unread. No average, substitution or promotion is performed.
follow_up: Reading Hagiyama et al. 2008 would settle whether the 107 compilation value has a primary measurement behind it and at which temperature it was measured.
Table 2.4 of the same chapter lists compilation-level values for EC 90 (40 C), PC 65, DME 5.5 and others; it was not used to change any dataset row.
